title: Measured maximal heart rates compared to commonly used age-based prediction equations in the HERITAGE Family Study
claims: In 762 sedentary HERITAGE subjects, the standard error of estimate (SEE) of predicted maximal heart rate was 12.4 bpm for the Fox 220 − age formula and 11.4 bpm for the Tanaka 208 − 0.7 × age formula.
SEE was higher in Black participants (14.4/13.1 bpm) and male participants (12.6/11.7 bpm) than in White participants (11.0/10.2 bpm) and female participants (12.3/11.2 bpm).
The Fox formula is reported to have a SEE of 7–12 bpm.
Tanaka and colleagues reported a SEE of approximately 10 bpm for 208 − 0.7 × age.
Resting heart rate in the total HERITAGE sample was 65.4 bpm (standard deviation 9.1), with values ranging from 40.3 to 105.3 bpm.
The authors concluded that the prevailing age-based maximal heart rate equations do not precisely predict an individual's measured maximal heart rate.

claimVerification.note: 原文 Results：“Overall, the SEE was 12.4 and 11.4 bpm for the prediction of measured-HRmax using the Fox-HRmax and Tanaka-HRmax formulas, respectively.” 样本“762 sedentary subjects”见 Methods。

Table 2：“SEE of Fox-HRmax prediction”＝12.4（总）、11.0（White）、14.4（Black）、12.3（Female）、12.6（Male）；“SEE of Tanaka-HRmax prediction”＝11.4、10.2、13.1、11.2、11.7。正文：“The SEE of the prediction was greater in Blacks as compared to Whites for both formulas, with the Fox-HRmax formula in Blacks showing the largest SEE value of 14.4 bpm.”

原文引言：“The Fox et al. formula is known to be quite variable, with a standard error of estimate (SEE) of predicted HRmax of 7–12 beats per minute (bpm) (Robergs and Landwehr, 2002; Thompson, 2010).” claim 用“is reported to have”保留了转述语气。
原文引言：“the authors derived the following formula to predict HRmax: 208 – 0.7 × age, which was the same for both men and women, and had a SEE of ~10 bpm (Tanaka et al., 2001).”
Table 1 总样本：“Resting heart rate, bpm 65.4 (9.1) 40.3 to 105.3”。

原文结论：“our results fail to validate the effectiveness of either of the two most widely used age-based HRmax prediction equations in sedentary, healthy adults.” 摘要：“the prevailing age-based estimated HRmax equations do not precisely predict an individual’s measured-HRmax.” claim 的“do not precisely predict”与摘要逐字一致。
